30th. January 192 4.

REPORT ON Zung Ping Sung. President of Chinese Seamen's Union.

Made by D. S. Tinkler. Forwarded by [签名]

Sir,

In accordance with instructions, a Mixed Court warrant for the arrest of Zung Ping Sung was obtained on the 26/1/24 on the new charge of fraud, he having issued a native order on the 10/1/24 for $549.00 ( drawn on the Tuck Dah Bank and post-dated ten days as the others ) for provisions supplied to the Hai Shing Co. The complainants Messrs Yuen Tah and Co. Broadway were represented by Attorney M. L. Heen and wished to have the accountant of the Hai Shing Co ( Tsang Kya Ji ) included in the charge. Both names were accordingly included in the warrant.

Tsang Kya Ji was arrested at 5 p.m. on the 28/1/24 at 94, Broadway, taken before the Mixed Court on the 29/1/24 and remanded in custody until the 30/1/24. The Police are not interested to any extent in the prosecution of this man and the case against him will scarcely succeed as a criminal matter.

Zung Ping Sung failed to surrender himself on the 30/1/24 and the $600.00 bail was confiscated. On the application of Mr. Maitland, who appeared for the Police, an expulsion order was made against him.

Tsang Kya Ji was remanded on $600.00 shop or cash security till the 1/2/24. Counsel for complainants ( M. L. Heen for Messrs. Yuen Tah and Co.) will probably withdraw the case against him in the criminal court.

Every endeavour has been made to locate Zung Ping Sung, but without avail, and it is still uncertain whether he has left Shanghai or not. His wife is reported to have left for

關於中國海員公會會長陳炳生 (Zung Ping Sung) 的報告。

由 D. S. Tinkler 撰寫。由 [簽名] 轉呈

先生，

遵照指示，已於1924年1月26日就新的欺詐指控獲得了逮捕陳炳生 (Zung Ping Sung) 的會審公廨拘票，原因是他於1924年1月10日開具了一張金額為549.00美元的莊票（以德大銀行為付款行，並像其他票據一樣倒填日期十天），用於支付供應給海興公司的貨款。原告元泰洋行（百老匯路）由律師 M. L. Heen 代理，並希望將海興公司會計曾嘉祺 (Tsang Kya Ji) 列入指控對象。因此，兩人的名字均被列入拘票。

曾嘉祺 (Tsang Kya Ji) 於1924年1月28日下午5時在百老匯路94號被捕，於1924年1月29日被提審至會審公廨，並還押候審至1924年1月30日。警方對起訴此人並無多大興趣，且針對他的案件作為刑事案件很難成功。

陳炳生 (Zung Ping Sung) 未於1924年1月30日投案，600.00美元保釋金被沒收。根據代表警方出庭的梅特蘭 (Maitland) 先生的申請，已對他作出驅逐令。

曾嘉祺 (Tsang Kya Ji) 以600.00美元店鋪或現金擔保還押候審至1924年2月1日。原告律師（代表元泰洋行的 M. L. Heen）可能會在刑事法庭撤回對他的起訴。

已盡一切努力尋找陳炳生 (Zung Ping Sung) 的下落，但無果而終，目前仍不確定他是否已離開上海。據報其妻子已前往

25th. January 192 4.

REPORT ON Arrest of Zung Ping Sung. President of the Chinese
Seamen's Union.

Made by D. S. Tinkler. Forwarded by J. O'Boyle.

Sir,

Having received information that the Hai Shing
Compradore Shop, 94, Broadway ( of which Zung Ping Sung was
manager ) was indebted to Messrs Yuen Tah and Co. 111, Broadway
for wines and spirits supplied, I made enquiries and found that
Zung Ping Sung issued a worthless native order for $549.00
drawn on the Tuck Dah Native Bank, Seward Road.

Like the two previously mentioned, this order was
issued on the 10/1/24 and post-dated the 20/1/24. At the time of
issue there were no funds in the bank, but, on the 20/1/24 the
sum of Tls. 100.00 was deposited in favour of Zung Ping Sung.

A further $563.00 is owed by the Hai Shing Co. to
Messrs. Yuen Tah and Co. but this is a civil matter only.

Attorney M. L. Heen is now proceeding civilly
against Zung Ping Sung and is willing to take criminal
proceedings against Zung and his absconded accountant, Tseng
Kya Ji ( 張嘉祺 ) with respect to the worthless order.

The Civil Dept. of The Mixed Court has issued
sealing orders for the shop at 94, Broadway, but these have not
been executed by the Mixed Court as it is impossible to seal the
shop without obstructing the free passage of other sub-tenants
in the building.

Zung Ping Sung ( who has engaged Attorney Sellett
to defend him ) was released on the 24/1/24 on bail of $600.00,
the court on the previous day being inclined ( with reason ) to
view the charges against him as more of a civil than a criminal
nature.

關於逮捕中國海員公會會長陳炳生 (Zung Ping Sung) 的報告。

由 D. S. Tinkler 撰寫。由 J. O'Boyle 轉呈。

先生，

接到情報稱，百老匯路94號的海興買辦商店（陳炳生任經理）欠百老匯路111號元泰洋行供應的酒類貨款，我進行了查詢，發現陳炳生開具了一張金額為549.00美元的無效莊票，付款行為西華路德大華商银行。

與前述兩張票據一樣，這張票據於1924年1月10日開具，倒填日期為1924年1月20日。開票時銀行內沒有資金，但在1924年1月20日，有100.00兩白銀存入陳炳生賬戶。

海興公司還欠元泰洋行563.00美元，但這僅屬民事事項。

律師 M. L. Heen 現在正對陳炳生提起民事訴訟，並願意就該無效莊票對陳及其潛逃的會計曾嘉祺 (Tseng Kya Ji) ( 張嘉祺 ) 提起刑事訴訟。

會審公廨民事庭已對百老匯路94號的店鋪發出查封令，但會審公廨尚未執行這些命令，因為在不阻礙樓內其他分租戶自由通行的情況下無法查封該店鋪。

陳炳生（已聘請塞萊特 (Sellett) 律師為其辯護）於1924年1月24日以600.00美元保釋金獲釋，法院在前一天傾向於（有理由地）將對他的指控視為更具民事性質而非刑事性質。

REPORT ON ____________________ 2. ____________________

With regard to the worthless order issued to
Messrs. Yuen Tah and Co., I respectfully ask for instructions
as to which of the following courses of action to take.

It is possible to obtain another warrant on the
new charge and ( provided that same Assessor and Magistrate are
not opposed to it.) re-arrest Zung Ping Sung before the next
hearing of the case on the 30/1/24 ( I.e. as quickly as possible)
or, it is possible to wait and add this as a further charge
( criminal ) when the case goes up for hearing on the 30/1/24
without getting a warrant ( though, in the meantime, Zung Ping
Sung has every inducement to abscond and forfeit the $600.00
bail.)

The fact that Zung Ping Sung is represented by
counsel would seem to indicate that he intends to remain here
and fight the case in court.

Yours Obediently,
[Signature]
D. S.

P. S. The Civil Dept. of the Mixed Court has refused to issue
a Summons for Immediate Security against Zung Ping Sung.

關於向元泰洋行開具的無效莊票，我恭敬地請求指示，應採取以下哪種行動方案。

22nd. January. 192 4.

REPORT ON President of Chinese Seamens' Union Arrested For Fraud.

Made by D. S. Tinkler. Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

At 10 p.m. on the 22/1/24, a Cantonese tobacco dealer named Zung Tuh Ming (陳鏡明) of 131, Honan Road came to this station and reported that, on the 10/1/24, a Cantonese named Zung Ping Sung (陳炳生) manager of the Hai Shing Compradore Shop ( 海興 ), 94, Broadway, had given him a worthless native order ( for cigars etc. supplied.) for $300.00, drawn on the Tuck Dah Bank ( Woochang Seward Rds. Corner.). The order was issued on the 10/1/24 at 94, Broadway and was post-dated 20/1/24. On presenting the order for payment on the 20/1/24, the complt. found that Zung Ping Sung had no funds in the bank and had had no funds in it when he issued the order.

Zung Tuh Ming was accompanied by another complt., Zung Kyih Ying (陳吉英), manager of an egg company at 121, Yuenchang Road who had a similar order on the Tuck Dah Bank for $269.00 ( for a consignment of eggs ). This order was also issued on the 10/1 /24 and post-dated 20/1/24.

Zung Ping Sung is the President of the Chinese Seamens' Union, which has premises over the compradore shop at 94, Broadway.

On proceeding to that place to make enquiries re the matter ( at 10.15 p.m. 22/1/24 ) we found a meeting in progress at which more than twenty Cantonese were present, discussing the proceedings re the shooting etc. on the S. S. "Paul Regardanz".

Zung Ping Sung was requested to come to this station, and, on his admitting that he had no funds in the Tuck Dah Bank

關於中國海員公會會長因欺詐被捕的報告。

由 D. S. Tinkler 撰寫。由 [簽名] 轉呈

先生，

1924年1月22日晚上10點，河南路131號的一名廣東籍煙草商人名叫陳鏡明 (Zung Tuh Ming) 來到本捕房報案稱，1924年1月10日，百老匯路94號海興買辦商店 ( 海興 ) 經理、廣東人陳炳生 (Zung Ping Sung) 給了他一張金額為300.00美元的無效莊票（用於供應的雪茄等）。該票據以德大銀行（武昌路與西華路拐角處）為付款行。該票據於1924年1月10日在百老匯路94號開具，倒填日期為1924年1月20日。原告於1924年1月20日持票兌付時，發現陳炳生在銀行沒有資金，且在開票時也沒有資金。

陳鏡明由另一名原告陪同，即運昌路121號一家雞蛋公司的經理陳吉英 (Zung Kyih Ying)，他持有一張類似以德大銀行為付款行的莊票，金額為269.00美元（用於一批雞蛋）。這張票據也於1924年1月10日開具，倒填日期為1924年1月20日。

陳炳生是中國海員公會會長，該公會辦公處位於百老匯路94號買辦商店樓上。

當我們前往該地調查此事時（1924年1月22日晚上10點15分），我們發現正在舉行會議，有二十多名廣東人在場，討論關於“保爾·雷加丹茲”號 (S. S. "Paul Regardanz") 輪船槍擊事件等的訴訟程序。

要求陳炳生來本捕房，在他承認他在德大銀行沒有資金的情況下

The two complts. named have engaged a Chinese lawyer named W. H. Chen (陳漢明) to prosecute, but, as they did not do so until late this evening, no warrant was obtained. One of Zung Ping Sung's accountants has already absconded and both complainants feared that he would follow.
華昌 Whilst we were at 94, Broadway we met a Chinese named Zen Tahaung Zung, proprietor of a tobacco store on Broadway, to whom Zung Ping Sung owes $520.00 ( No order issued ). He was advised to sue civilly as soon as possible.
I understand that there are many other cases pending against Zung Ping Sung, but, at present am unable to say whether they are criminal or civil.

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, THURSDAY, JANUARY 31, 1924.

NO REFUGE FOR
MURDERER

MAN EXPELLED

Seamen's Leader Was
Pardoned By Dr. Sun

KILLED HIS WIFE

Still another place in the Far
East has refused to harbour
Chang Ping-sang, former pre-
sident of the Chinese National
Seamen's Union, who murdered
his wife in Canton in 1922 but
was pardoned by Dr. Sun Yat-
sen.
An expulsion order was grant-
ed by the Mixed Court yester-
day. Although Chang did not
put in an appearance to answer
four charges of fraud against
him, his presence in the Settle-
ment will no longer be tolerated.
The case in which Chang
figured so prominently was a
cause celebre during the seamen's
strike originating in Hongkong
in the early part of 1922. He
was president of the Seamen's
Union, and was sentenced to
12 years' imprisonment for
murdering his wife, and shoot-
ing one policeman dead, and
wounding several others who
tried to arrest him. Although
he was convicted and found
guilty everyone was surprised to
learn in May, 1922, that Dr. Sun
had pardoned him. The an-
nouncement of the pardon let
loose a storm of disapproval and
criticism of Dr. Sun's administra-
tion.
Chang left for Hongkong,
where he intended settling, but
he was denied refuge. He was
banished from the Colony for ten
years. He came to Shanghai, in
connection with the Chinese
National Seamen's Union, which
has a flourishing branch here.
Chang fell foul of the police
and was charged with obtaining
wines and provisions by fraud.

《字林西报》，1924年1月31日，星期四。

凶手无处藏身

男子被驱逐出境

海员领袖曾获孙博士赦免

杀害其妻

远东又有一地拒绝容留陈炳生，此人系前中华全国海员工会主席，曾于1922年在广州杀害其妻，但获孙中山博士赦免。
昨日，混合法庭签发了驱逐令。尽管陈炳生未出庭应诉针对他的四项欺诈指控，但公共租界将不再容忍其逗留。
陈炳生在其中扮演重要角色的案件，是1922年初起源于香港的海员罢工期间的一桩轰动性案件。他当时担任海员工会主席，因杀害其妻、枪杀一名警察并打伤数名试图逮捕他的警察而被判处12年监禁。虽然他被定罪并判定有罪，但令人惊讶的是，大家在1922年5月得知孙博士已赦免了他。赦免令的发布引发了对孙博士行政管理的强烈不满和批评浪潮。
陈炳生前往香港，打算在那里定居，但被拒绝收容。他被驱逐出该殖民地十年。他来到上海，与在此设有繁荣分支机构的中华全国海员工会有关。陈炳生与警方发生冲突，并被指控通过欺诈手段获取酒类和食品。

Precis

Hai Hing & Co.
94 Broadway Road,
S H A N G H A I.
7th, November, 1923.

Mr. Hon Ki,

I have received your letter stating that you seconded my proposal to establish this Co. This Co. has been established for half a month. It would be fortunate enough if you will put up some shares in the business. Please send the share-money here at an earlier date as it should be paid up before the 10th day of the 10th moon(i.e.22.11.23). Now the number of shares has been filled up.

I have learnt in Shanghai that you had trouble with Mr So (i.e.So Sin Ching) in Canton and that the Generalissimo has issued an order for your arrest. I don't know if it is a fact. I have not seen any report to that effect made by the Union nor have I received any letter from you mentioning same. Please tell me whether it is true.

Several months ago I declared that all the present working officers should be dismissed in the coming term. I am now elected to continue the office for the coming term. I have determined not to receive it. It is very difficult to manage the society business as there is no spirit for the work now. This is the reason that I leave the service to establish the Hai Hing Co.

With compliments,
(sd) CHAN PING SANG.

海兴公司

韩基先生：

收到来信，知悉您附议我建立该公司的提议。该公司已成立半个月。若您能入股，将是幸事。请于较早日期将股金汇至此处，因为应在农历十月初十（即1923年11月22日）之前缴清。目前股份已满额。

我在上海听说您在广州与苏先生（即苏辛清）发生纠纷，且大元帅已签发逮捕您的命令。不知是否属实。我未见工会对此有任何报告，也未收到您提及此事的来信。请告知我这是否属实。

数月前我曾宣布，所有现任干事应在下一届任期被解职。我现在当选连任下一届职务。我已决定不接受。由于目前缺乏工作热情，管理会社事务非常困难。这就是我离职创办海兴公司的原因。

此致，
（签名）陈炳生。

Sir,

THE CHINA PRESS, SATURDAY, MAY 6, 1922

Dr. Sun Pardons
Strike Leader
(Reuter Pacific Service)
Hongkong, May 5.—Chan Ping-sang, ex-president of the Seamen's Union, who was sentenced to 12 years imprisonment at Canton for the murder of his wife, has been pardoned and liberated by Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
A crowd of laborers, who had gathered outside the prison gate, cheered the Labor leader upon his emergence from the gaol.
Commenting on Chan's liberation, the Hongkong Daily Press states, in the course of an editorial article: "Most people will read with amazement the news that Dr. Sun Yat-sen has granted a free pardon to Chan Ping-sang. The murder was a particularly cold-blooded one. The release of the murderer from the punishment imposed by the Court reflects no credit either on the Executive or the people who rejoice in this act of incredible leniency, unequalled since Barabbas escaped crucifixion."
The South China Morning Post states: "Nothing will justify such a scandalous precedent in the eyes of thinking and genuinely patriotic Chinese, who will see in it not only a handle for China's external enemies, but a highly dangerous expedient, likely to threaten the authority of all civil law."

孙博士赦免
罢工领袖
（路透社太平洋分社）
香港，5月5日电。——前海员工会主席陈炳生（Chan Ping-sang），此前因谋杀妻子在广州被判处12年监禁，现已被孙逸仙博士赦免并释放。
聚集在监狱门外的一群劳工，在该劳工领袖走出监狱时向他欢呼。
《香港日报》在一篇社论中评论陈炳生的获释时称：“大多数人读到孙逸仙博士给予陈炳生完全赦免的消息时都会感到惊讶。这起谋杀案特别冷血。将凶手从法院判处的刑罚中释放，既不能为行政当局增光，也不能为那些对这种令人难以置信的宽大行为感到高兴的人们增光，这种宽大自巴拉巴（Barabbas）逃脱十字架之刑以来尚属首次。”
《南华早报》称：“在有思想且真正爱国的中国人眼中，没有任何理由能为如此可耻的先例辩护，他们不仅会从中看到中国外部敌人的把柄，还会看到一种极有可能威胁所有民法权威的极度危险的权宜之计。”

SHANGHAI, WEDNESDAY, FEBRUARY 22, 1922.

Chinese Seamen's
Head Held For
Murder

Chan Ping Sang, Chairman of the Seamen's Union has been arrested Canton on a charge of murdering his wife.
The story of the crime as it is related in the Vernacular Press reads as follows:
While walking near the foot of the Pak Wan mountain, on the 14th instant, a man discovered a young woman lying unconscious beneath a bush with several serious wounds on her body. He at once reported the matter to the nearest police station. The wounds were so serious that the woman died an hour after she had been brought to the station. According to her dying deposition, she said that she was assassinated by the husband, Chan Ping Sang, President of the Chinese Seamen's Union, who was staying with a friend (also an unofficial of the Union) in the Yuet Wah Hotel on the Bund. As her husband fell in love with a girl and did not support her, she purposely on the 13th went up to Canton from Hongkong to find him and they had some quarrels. On the day when the murder took place, she was persuaded to make a trip to the Pak Wan mountain. The friend of her husband accompanied them. When they arrived at the foot of the mountain, her husband suddenly drew out a pistol and fired several shots at her.
On this information a squad of policemen and detectives was despatched to the Yuet Wah Hotel to arrest the alleged murderer. When they reached the hotel Chan was out but returned in a short while and the officer in charge of the police squad produced to him the warrant for his arrest. He at once drew out a pistol and fired point blank at the policemen and at the same time tried to escape but after a short chase he was arrested Two police were wounded by shots fired by Chan, the condition of one being very critical.
At the police headquarters Chan confessed that he murdered his wife and said that his friend, who was one of the party, had nothing to do with the murder.
At the time of his arrest several seamen came to his assistance, but after the police had explained to them that the matter was personal and there was nothing concerning the Union the seamen dispersed.

上海，1922年2月22日，星期三。

中国海员
首领因谋杀
被捕

海员工会主席陈炳生（Chan Ping Sang）因涉嫌谋杀其妻子在广州被捕。
中文报刊报道的案情如下：
本月14日，一名男子在白万山（Pak Wan mountain，音译）脚下附近行走时，发现一名年轻女子昏迷躺在灌木丛下，身上有多处重伤。他立即向最近的警察局报告此事。伤势过重，该女子在被送往警局一小时后死亡。据其临终证词，她说自己是被丈夫、中国海员工会主席陈炳生所刺杀，当时陈正与一位朋友（也是工会的一名非正式官员）住在外滩的粤华酒店（Yuet Wah Hotel）。由于丈夫爱上了一名女孩且不再供养她，她特意于13日从香港前往广州寻找他，双方发生了一些争吵。案发当天，她被劝诱前往白万山游览。她丈夫的朋友陪同他们同行。当他们到达山脚时，她的丈夫突然掏出手枪，向她连开数枪。
根据这一情报，一队警察和侦探被派往粤华酒店逮捕这名涉嫌凶手。当他们到达酒店时，陈不在，但不久后返回，警队负责人向他出示了逮捕令。他立即掏出手枪，近距离向警察开枪，同时试图逃跑，但在短暂追逐后被捕。两名警察被陈开枪击伤，其中一人情况非常危急。
在警察总局，陈承认谋杀了其妻子，并称同行的朋友与谋杀案无关。
在他被捕时，几名海员前来协助他，但在警察向他们解释此事属于个人事务，与工会无关后，海员们便散去了。

FREEDOM OF THE
PRESS
Mixed Court Refuses To
Grant Injunction
The Mixed Court yesterday
refused to grant an injunction
against nine Chinese newspapers
restraining them from publishing
certain alleged libellous articles.

of the China Merchants' Steam-

legations against the company,
had been issued in the form of
a pamphlet, by unknown persons,

made reference to it. Mr. Foo
of the company called at the
offices of the "Sin Wan Pao"

the contents of the pamphlet as
it might cause serious trouble,
but his request was refused on
the grounds that the matter
was of public interest.
Mr. Mead, the British Assess-

observed that if the court issued
an injunction it might lead to
complications. He did not want
to restrict the freedom of the
press, and he was sure the papers
concerned knew the consequences
of publication of libellous artic-
les.

混合法庭昨日拒绝颁发针对九家中文报纸的禁令，以限制其发表某些涉嫌诽谤的文章。
该申请由R. N. Macleod先生代表轮船招商局提出。
为支持该申请，律师告知法庭，一些不明身份的人以小册子的形式发布了一份请愿书，对公司提出某些指控，中文报刊对此进行了引用。该公司的Foo先生（音译）走访了《新闻报》（Sin Wan Pao）报社，要求他们不要刊登小册子的内容，因为这可能会引起严重麻烦，但该请求以事关公共利益为由被拒绝。
英国陪审官Mead先生驳回了该申请，他指出，如果法庭颁发禁令，可能会导致复杂局面。他不想限制新闻自由，并且确信相关报纸知道发表诽谤文章的后果。

Sir,
The facts contained in the attached report prove conclusively that a branch office of the Chinese Seamen's Union was established at the Chung Hwa Leu (中華樓) Teashop, Chinese Bund. Moreover since the seamen's strike a split has occurred in the ranks of the Union with the result that the Lien Yi Shao (聯益社) Cooks, Stewards, and Boys Union have seceded from the Chinese Seamen's Union and litigation is in progress in the Mixed Court between the parties. When making enquiries into the matter I was informed by Yih Kuh Lai (葉來) an organiser of the Chinese Seamen's Union, Shanghai Branch, that Tsu Zu Zai (朱如才) President of the Lien Yi Shao Cooks, Stewards and Boys Union was one of the most energetic workers for the Union during the strike and that he was then in charge of the branch office at the Chung Hwa Leu (中華樓) teashop, Yih further stated that jealousy on the part of Tsu Zu Zai had caused the split in the Union.

The branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union at the Chung Hwa Leu (中華樓) teashop, Nantao Bund was visited by Police agents while meetings of seamen were in progress there.
As a result of information supplied from this office the Chinese Police visited the teashop on August 16, and removed the Seamen's Union's flags and posters and dispersed a large number of seamen who had assembled there.
After that date seamen on strike continued to assemble at the teashop and committee men of the Union visited there twice daily, in the forenoon and afternoon.
Luk Sheung Kut (陸常吉) one of the five men who came from Hongkong to Shanghai to organize the Seamen's Union attended at the teashop regularly and on August 19, he gave his card, attached, to a police agent. The striking seamen continued to assemble at the Chung Hwa Leu (中華樓) teashop right up to the termination of the strike and the thirty cents per day granted to the strikers by the Union was distributed there.
I am, Sir,
Your Obedient Servant,
J. Sullivan.,
D. I.

REPORT ON A Review of the Recent Seamen's Strike.

Made by D.I. Sullivan. Forwarded by [Signature] for Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir:
The following is a brief review of the strike of seamen which terminated on August 25. Following a general strike of seamen, which ultimately embraced almost all branches of labour which started in Hongkong on January 13 and terminated on March 5 and which resulted in men employed in all branches of the seafaring profession receiving increases of pay, five representatives of the Hongkong branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union named Lam Wai Man (林偉民), Chun Shui Pang, (鐘筱朋) Wong Sou Yat (黃守一) Luk Sheung Kat (陸常吉) and Ip Kip Lai (葉謁来) arrived in Shanghai on May 18 and at once started to organize a Shanghai branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union with offices at 163 Broadway. The organizers were guided in everything they did by a lawyer whose services were retained by the Union.

The Shanghai branch of the Seamen's Union sent letters to a number of shipping firms on July 23, July 31, and August 4 asking that the pay of the crews of their ships be raised to the same level as that granted after the strike at Hongkong. The request of the Union did not effect the large shipping firms in Shanghai who had anticipated the Union's demands and raised the pay of their crews immediately after the settlement of the Hongkong strike, with the single exception of the China Merchants S. N. Co. who only raised the pay of the crews of five of their ships which were employed on the Hongkong run. The Marine Superintendent

虽然这不影响中国海员工会的法律地位，但事实仍然是，考虑到近期航运界的事件，招商局轮船公司陷入目前的处境只能怪自己。首先，在香港罢工平息后，该公司的海事监督曾警告董事们，只提高部分船舶船员的工资而不提高其他船舶船员的工资是一个错误，这必然会导致进一步的麻烦。
其次，当中国海员工会在上海初建时，招商局轮船公司的管理层必定知道，由于他们未向船员支付增加的工资，他们将成为工会攻击的大型公司中的第一家。

CHINESE SEAMEN'S UNION, HONGKONG.
----------

There is no restriction on the formation or
existence of any Society in Hongkong, as a Society;
under the limitations only of Ordinance No. 8 of 1889,
and of course the general laws of the Colony. The
Seamen's Union does not fall within the limitations
and can exist and function as long as it does not
otherwise offend.

It has one special privilege under the
Strike Agreement: of explaining Articles to its
own members at signing. The privilege does not
cover others than its own members: but their
assistance would not be objected to if the men
signing asked for it.

It is not the only Seamen's Union in the
Colony: e.g. THE HONG HOI LUN HOP KUNG WUI, is separate
and independent & represents a breaking-away from the
Union of a large number of men. A number of
Boarding-houses also are independent of the Union,
and some new ones are opening for the purpose of
being clear of its influence.

I have the honour to be,
Sir,
Your obedient servant,
(Signed) E. D. Wolfe
Capt: Supt: of Police.

The Commissioner,
Municipal Police,
Shanghai.

香港中国海员工会。
----------

在香港，任何社团的成立或存在均不受限制，作为一个社团；仅受1889年第8号条例的限制，当然还受殖民地一般法律的约束。海员工会不属于这些限制范围，只要不触犯其他法律，即可存在并运作。

根据罢工协议，它享有一项特权：在签署时向其会员解释条款。该特权不适用于其会员以外的人：但如果签字的人员请求协助，对其提供帮助也不会被反对。

它并非殖民地唯一的海员工会：例如，洪海联和公会是独立且分离的，代表了大量人员从该工会中分裂出来。许多寄宿寓所也独立于该工会，一些新开的寓所旨在摆脱其影响。

The following are the conditions of settlement
agreed upon between the Chinese Seamen's Union
(Shanghai Branch) and the China Merchants S. N. Co.
(1) The crews of all ocean and river steamers
except the 5 steamers on the Hankow run, will
receive an increase of 20% in wages.
(2) The increase to take effect from May 1, 1922.
(3) The crews of all steamers to be paid full
wages for the period of the strike.
(4) In future the signing of engagements
between the China Merchants S. N. Co. and seamen
must be witnessed by a representative of the
Seamen's Union, otherwise the contracts will be
declared null and void.
(5) The company will immediately dismiss any
seaman who commits an unlawful act. If the seaman
dismissed is dissatisfied, a joint investigation
by the Seamen's Union and the China Merchants S.N.Co.
will be held, and if the company is found to be in
the wrong, the complainant will be taken back
in his original position and paid his full wages.

REPORT ON The financial position of the Chinese Seamen's
Union, Shanghai Branch

Made by       D. I. Sullivan      Forwarded by [签名] Director of Intelligence.

Sir,

    Whilst making enquiries at the Chinese Seamen's
Union's headquarters, 165 Broadway, into the case of a
threatening letter sent to an employee of the China Merchants
S. N. Co., I was informed by Yih Kuh Lai(葉謁来), one
of the men who came to Shanghai from Hongkong to form the
Shanghai branch of the Union, that only three hundred
seamen have paid their subscription to the Shanghai branch
of the Union. There are a large number of names of seamen
on the books whose subscriptions the Union expect to
receive when the present strike is settled, and there are
also a large number of men employed on ships running to
Southern ports who are members of the Hongkong and Canton
branches of the Union. Some of the three hundred paid up
members have paid $5.60 each which entitles them to a
certificate of membership for 1921 and 1922, and some
have paid $3.40 each which entitled them to a certificate
for 1922 only.

    When asked how the Union is kept going with such
a small paying membership, my informant answered that when
the organizers of the Shanghai branch left Hongkong they
were given $500.00 by the Hongkong branch of the Union.
Six local seamen's guilds subscribed $200.00 each making
$1,200.00 to the Chinese Seamen's Union.

    The crews of some ocean going ships have
subscribed, for instance the crew of the S.S. "President
Madison" subscribed $85.00.

The S.S. "Yushun" of the China Merchants S. N. Co.
arrived in Shanghai from Chefoo on August 22. The crew left
the steamer as soon as she arrived. This brings the total
of the company's steamers which are idle to twenty four.

About seventy seamen assembled at the headquarters
of the Seamen's Union, 165 Broadway, on the afternoon of
August 22. They were addressed by Cheong Dang Lai (慶順來),
a Cantonese member of the committee of the Chinese Seamen's
Union, Shanghai branch, and a man named Loh Hoiem (陸軒),
a Cantonese who has recently arrived in Shanghai from Hong-
kong. He was formerly one of the crew of the S.S. "Hoosier
State", but is now in the employ of the Chung Hwa Tobacco Co.
Hongkong. Both speakers advised their hearers to be
patient and said that the China Merchants S. N. Co. would be
bound to submit to the Union's demands. The meeting was
very orderly and quiet, and there was no cheering or
applause in fact it would be difficult to say from the
attitude of the strikers who were present whether they were
enthusiastic in support of the strike or not.

The Directors of the China Merchants S. N. Co. held
a meeting on August 23 and discussed the strike situation.

    Zee Siao Pee(徐小比), alias Zee Tsong Sing

and Nantao, and of the Sai Kaung(三江) Steamship Co.,
Nantao Bund, was seriously assaulted on the Nantao Bund on

    It appears that Zee went from his house at
2 Rue Takua at about 8 a.m. to a firm called Yeong Lee
(永記) on Nantao Bund on business. On leaving the premises
of the Yeong Lee(永記) firm which are situated in an
alleyway off Nantao Bund and whilst proceeding to his private
ricksha which was waiting on the Nantao Bund, he was approached
by four men who took hold of him and started to punch him.
Zee who is a strong man put up a struggle whereupon five or
six more men came from behind. One of the men had a pair
of scissors with which he cut off the top part of Zee's
right ear. Zee says he could identify four or five of the
men if he saw them again. He also states that he has
seen some of his assailants loafing about the place for
some days. A member of the Nantao Police Force came upon the
scene but the men had already escaped. The affair has been
reported to the Nantao Police.

    I saw the injured man at the Paulun Hospital,
Burkill Road, on the afternoon of August 15. He was
formerly a boatswain in the employ of the China Merchants
Ss Na Co. but left them some years ago to start his own

August 16th 1922.

The Marine Superintendent,
Dear Sir:
    We understand that you and the masters and officers of the vessels belonging to the China Merchants' steamship navigation Company are bringing pressure to bear upon the Chinese Seamen who are now on strike. We wish to emphasise the following facts:
    1.- That your Company signed the agreement of March 8th last in Hongkong which made the increase retrospective as from January 1st 1922.
    2.- That with exception of your Company all other Companies both Chinese and Foreign who were parties to that agreement have recognised it is binding in Shanghai.
    3.- That the men are asking for nothing more than they are fairly entitled to.
    4.- That your Company is a Chinese Company and before all should in fairness be ready to treat their fellow country men with the same amount of justice as Foreign Companies have done.
    5.- That the prolongation of this strike will not only lead to enormous losses to all parties concerned but will seriously affect the trade of those ports to and from which your Company run their steamers.
    Finally we would point out that the mercantile marine officers on the Chinese Coast only secured an increase of pay for themselves by methods precisely similar to those adopted by the Chinese seamen.
    Trusting you will see your way to use your good offices to effect a favourable settlement, as, after all, the seamen follow the calling of sea as much as the masters and officers.
                                We are, Gentlemen, yours faithfully,
                                (Sgd) Lam Wei Nan

1922年8月17日

致海事总监先生：

敬启者：

据悉，阁下及招商局轮船所属船只的船长和高级船员，正向目前罢工的中国海员施加压力。我们要强调以下事实：

1. 贵公司已于去年3月8日在香港签署协议，规定加薪自1922年1月1日起追溯生效。
2. 除贵公司外，所有签署该协议的其他中外公司均已承认该协议在上海具有约束力。
3. 海员们的要求并未超出其应得的合理范围。
4. 贵公司是一家中国公司，理应首先秉持公平原则，像外国公司那样公正地对待本国同胞。
5. 此次罢工的延长不仅将给有关各方带来巨大损失，还将严重影响贵公司轮船往来港口的贸易。

最后，我们要指出，中国沿海商船的高级船员正是通过与中国海员所采取的完全相同的方法，才为自己争取到了加薪。

相信阁下会设法运用您的影响力促成有利的解决，毕竟，海员与船长及高级船员一样，都是以航海为业。

此致

Shanghai, 16 Aug., 1922.

The Marine Superintendent,

Dear Sir,

We understand that you and the masters
and officers of the vessels belonging to the China
Merchants Steam Nav. Co. are bringing pressure to bear
upon the Chinese seamen who are now on strike. We wish
to emphasize the following facts :-
(1) That your company signed the agreement of March 8
last in Hongkong which made the increase retrospective
as from Jan. 1, 1922.
(2) That with the exception of your company all other
companies both Chinese and Foreign who were parties to
that agreement have recognized it is binding in
Shanghai.
(3) That the men are asking for nothing more than they
are fairly entitled to.
(4) That your company is a Chinese company and before all
should in fairness be ready to treat their fellow-
countrymen with the same amount of justice as Foreign
companies have done.
(5) That the prolongation of this strike will not only
lead to enormous losses to all parties concerned,
but will seriously affect the trade of these ports to
which your company run their steamers.

Finally we would point out that the mercantile
marine officers in the Chinese Coast only secured an increase
of pay for themselves by a scale precisely similar
to that asked by the Chinese seamen.

Trusting you will see your way to use your good

上海，1922年8月16日。

致海事总监先生：

敬启者：

据悉，阁下及招商局轮船公司所属船只的船长和高级船员，正向目前罢工的中国海员施加压力。我们要强调以下事实：

(1) 贵公司已于去年3月8日在香港签署协议，规定加薪自1922年1月1日起追溯生效。
(2) 除贵公司外，所有签署该协议的其他中外公司均已承认该协议在上海具有约束力。
(3) 海员们的要求并未超出其应得的合理范围。
(4) 贵公司是一家中国公司，理应首先秉持公平原则，像外国公司那样公正地对待本国同胞。
(5) 此次罢工的延长不仅将给有关各方带来巨大损失，还将严重影响贵公司轮船往来这些港口的贸易。

最后，我们要指出，中国沿海商船的高级船员正是通过与中国海员所要求的完全相同的标准，才为自己争取到了加薪。

相信阁下会设法运用您的良好

the seamen follow the calling of the sea as much as
the masters and officers.
We are, Gentlemen,
Yours respectfully,

CHINA.
August 16 2

XXXXXXXX Daily Report

D. I. Sullivan
Sir,

There is no change in the strike situation
between the China Merchants S. N. Co. and the Chinese Seamen's
Union. Nineteen of the company's steamers are tied up in
Shanghai.

About 60 seamen assembled at the headquarters of
the Chinese Seamen's Union, 165 Broadway, at 4 p.m. August 15.
The assembly was addressed by Mr. Lin (林偉民),
President of the Union, who told his audience that they
must hold out to the last and if the China Merchants refuse
to come to an agreement with the Seamen's Union, the Union
will take the strikers to Hongkong where the Union will house and
support them and assist them to obtain employment. He
explained that if the China Merchants S. N. Co. are success-
ful in resisting the Union the other companies will break
their agreements and the pay of seamen will be reduced to
the old scale. A similar speech similar in tone was
delivered by Mr. Chen (陸希吉), a native of Macao
and a committee man of the Union. The meeting terminated
at 6 p.m.

A letter has been sent by the General
Directors of the China Merchants S. N. Co. to all captains
of the company's steamers in Shanghai telling the captains
that the company are willing to raise the pay of their
crews by $5.00 per month or more. This brings the scale
of wages up to the maximum rate and the only points
remaining are the demands of the Seamen's Union that the

Mr. Su Tuh Taz(須德子),
Head Coolie,
China Merchants S. N. Co.
Dear Sir,
The present action of our branch
in demanding wage increases is taken in order
to maintain the livelihood of our fellow workers
and to relieve the difficulties of labourers.
To our surprise, some of the steamship companies
ignored our request without sympathy. Consequently
we were reluctantly compelled to declare a
strike with a view to reaching a settlement.
You are one of the workmen, and therefore
are requested to render your practical assistance
and take unanimous action.
Stamp of Chinese Seamen's Union,
Shanghai Branch.

August 15 S

XXXXXXXXXXXX Daily Report

D. I. Sullivan

Sir,

The Chairman of Directors of the China Merchants
S. N. Co. asked the boatswains and head firemen of the ships,
the crews of which are on strike, to go to the company's
office at 5.30 p.m. August 14 to discuss the question of wages.
The men declined the invitation and as a result about 150
strikers assembled at the headquarters of the Chinese
Seamen's Union, 165 Broadway, at 3 p.m. August 14. Lam Hoi
Ming( ), President of the Chinese Seamen's Union,
Shanghai Branch, addressing the assembly said that he had
heard that the China Merchants S. N. Co. had asked the
Captains of their ships to induce the crews to return to
work. He asked those present what they intended to do.
The men decided unanimously not to return to work unless an
agreement is first signed between the C.M.S.N. Co. and the
Chinese Seamen's Union and not to accept individual invita-
tions to the C. M. S. N. Co.'s offices to discuss the strike.

The San Poh S. N. Co. and the Chinese Seamen's
Union reached an agreement at about 6 p.m. August 14 and
the crews of the company's ships have resumed work.

It is reported that a letter has been sent from
the Chinese Seamen's Union to the head wharf coolies employed
on the China Merchants S. N. Co.'s wharves asking the
wharf employees to come out on strike if the company refuse
to meet the demands of the seamen. The wharf coolies are
still working on the company's ships and if the seamen's
strike is not settled soon the wharf coolies will be idle as
there will be no work for them to do.

虞洽卿 (Yu Ya Ching) 先生。双方讨论了
海员的要求，但未能达成一致。
海员工会的官员并不太重视
三北轮船公司的态度，因为他们认为，一旦
招商局轮船公司表现出与海员工会谈判的迹象，
三北轮船公司就会达成妥协安排。

12/8/22

CENTRAL
August 12 2

XXXXXX-XXXX Daily Report

D.I. Sullivan

Sir,

The crew of the S.S. "Agnes Dollar" who struck
work on August 8 resumed work on the forenoon of August 11
on being granted an increase of 20% as from August 5.
The increase given does not raise the crews' wages to the
Hongkong Scale. The company in giving this increase state
that they mainly did so in order to carry out their contract
with Messrs Kunst & Albers to whom the steamer is chartered.
No agreement was signed with the Seamen's Union, the crew
signing their new articles in the presence of Mr. J. T.
Wright, Vice Consul of the United States Consulate Shipping
Office as is always done. Tsoong Siau Bang(鐘筱明), the
Vice President of the Seamen's Union was present on the
steamer at the time the articles were signed and mentioned
that he would call at the company's office with regard to the
latter signing an agreement with the Seamen's Union. The
company, however, state that they have no intention of
signing any such agreement. The date of sailing of the
"Agnes Dollar" is not yet fixed but it will probably leave
within the next two or three days.

Two more steamers of the China Merchants S. N.
Co.'s fleet viz :- the s.s. "Taichun" and "Kiangwah"
arrived in Shanghai on August 11 and on arrival the
crews immediately struck work. This makes altogether
nineteen of this company's vessels tied up and in addition
four of the San Poh S. N. Co.'s vessels are idle in this
port.

4652
1922年8月12日

中央巡捕房
1922年8月12日

XXXXXX-XXXX 日报

督察长沙利文（Sullivan）

阁下：

“Agnes Dollar”号轮船船员于8月8日罢工，在获准自8月5日起加薪20%后，已于8月11日上午复工。此次加薪并未使船员工资达到香港标准。公司在给予此次加薪时声明，其主要目的是为了履行与Kunst & Albers公司（音译）的合同，该轮船已租予该公司。公司未与海员工会签署任何协议，船员像往常一样在美国领事馆航运处副领事J. T. Wright先生面前签署了新的雇佣合同。海员工会副会长钟筱明（Tsoong Siau Bang）在签署合同时在场，并提及他将前往公司办公室，就后者与海员工会签署协议一事进行商谈。然而，公司表示无意签署此类协议。“Agnes Dollar”号的启航日期尚未确定，但可能会在未来两三天内离港。

招商局船队中的另外两艘轮船，即“Taichun”号（音译）和“Kiangwah”号（音译），于8月11日抵达上海，船员抵港后立即罢工。至此，该公司共有十九艘船只停泊，此外，三北轮埠公司（San Poh S. N. Co.）的四艘船只也在本港闲置。

page_data.en:
A meeting was held in the Seamen's Union offices, 105
Broadway, at 8 p.m. August 11 which was attended by about
100 strikers and which was presided over by Lam Wai Ming
(林偉民), President of the local branch of the Seamen's
Union. The gathering was addressed by Tseong Siau Beng
(鐘筱明), Secretary of the local branch of the Union, and
Loh Sang Kyih(隆帝吉), a member of the committee. The
latter is a native of Ningpo but came to Shanghai from
Hongkong to assist in the organization of the local branch
of the Seamen's Union. The speakers said that it had come
to their knowledge that efforts were being made to effect a
split between those members of the Union who are natives
of Ningpo and those who are natives of Canton. They urged
their hearers to remain united and not to destroy their
chances of success by secession from the Union's ranks.
A circular which will be distributed to seamen is in prepara-
tion by the Union.
Yu Ya Ching(虞洽卿), Managing Director of the
San Peh Te H. Co. and Hong On S. & Co. has written to the
Seamen's Union referring them to the companies' lawyer with
whom negotiations regarding the present dispute may be
carried on.
page_data.zh:
8月11日晚8时，在海员工会办公室（百老汇路105号）举行了一次会议，约有100名罢工者参加，由海员工会上海分会会长林伟民（Lam Wai Ming）主持。海员工会上海分会秘书钟筱明（Tseong Siau Beng）和委员会委员隆帝吉（Loh Sang Kyih，音译）向与会者发表了讲话。后者是宁波人，但从香港来到上海，协助组织海员工会上海分会。发言者称，他们获悉有人企图在海员工会中制造宁波籍会员与广东籍会员之间的分裂。他们敦促听众保持团结，不要因脱离工会队伍而破坏成功的机会。工会正在准备一份将分发给海员的通告。

三北泰兴公司（San Peh Te H. Co.）和鸿安轮船公司（Hong On S. & Co.）的总经理虞洽卿（Yu Ya Ching）致函海员工会，指引他们与公司律师联系，以便就目前的纠纷进行谈判。

GENERAL
August 11 2

XXXXXXXXXX Daily Report

D. 1. Sullivan

Sir,

The crews of steamers belonging to the China
Merchants S. N. Co. and the San Poh Steamship Co. are still
on strike. Two steamers of the company first named and
one from the second named arrived in Shanghai on August 10
and the crews immediately came ashore. There are now
seventeen of the C. I. S. N. Co.'s and four of the San Poh
S. N. Co.'s steamers laid up.

A committee meeting of the Ningpo Fellow Country
Men's Association was held at the Association, No. 4A Tibet
Road, at 4.30 p.m. August 10. Twelve members of the committee
including Yu Yah Ching(虞洽卿), Managing Director of
Hong On and San Poh S. N. Co., Wong Chro Pah(方椒伯),
Vice Chairman of the Chinese General Chamber of Commerce,
Yuen Li Tung(袁履登), ex-President of the Old Amalgamated
Association of Street Unions, attended. During the meeting
eight members of the Chung An Sailors Association (American
Trust), 550 Yuenfong Road, 34 members from the branches of
the Guild of Steamship Firemen situated respectively at 94
Pearson Road, 2082A Wu Lin; Lee(武林里), East Yuheng Road,
and 16 Tuen Zang Lee(登上里), Boulevards des Deux Republi-
ques, who are on strike, were told by the committee that wage
questions should be settled between the local firemen and
sailors guilds and the steam ship owners and that they
should have nothing to do with the Seamen's Union from
Hongkong. The meeting lasted at 7 p.m. but nothing of a
definite nature was done.

1922年8月11日

总巡捕房
1922年8月11日

XXXXXXXXXX 日报

督察长沙利文（Sullivan）

阁下：

招商局轮船公司（China Merchants S. N. Co.）和三北轮埠公司（San Poh Steamship Co.）所属轮船的船员仍在罢工。上述第一家公司有两艘轮船，第二家公司有一艘轮船，于8月10日抵达上海，船员随即上岸。目前，招商局轮船公司有十七艘轮船停航，三北轮埠公司有四艘轮船停航。

8月10日下午4时30分，宁波同乡会在同乡会会所（西藏路4A号）召开委员会会议。十二名委员出席，包括鸿安轮船公司和三北轮埠公司总经理虞洽卿（Yu Yah Ching）、上海总商会副会长方椒伯（Wong Chro Pah，音译）、旧各业公会联合会前主席袁履登（Yuen Li Tung）。会议期间，委员会告知均安水手公所（美商信托）（Chung An Sailors Association (American Trust)，源丰路550号）的八名成员，以及分别位于皮尔逊路94号、东余杭路武林里2082A号、两共和大道登上里（Tuen Zang Lee，音译）16号的轮船司炉公会所属分支机构的三十四名罢工成员，工资问题应由当地司炉和水手公会与轮船业主之间解决，他们不应与来自香港的海员工会发生任何关系。会议持续至晚上7时，但未达成任何实质性结果。

page_data.en:
The crew of the S.S. "Agnes Dollar" which arrived in
Shanghai on August 5 and which is now under charter to Messrs
Kunst & Albers, Vladivostock, went out on strike on August 8,
whilst she was undergoing repairs at the Kiangnan Dock.
All attempts by the company to sign a new crew have been
without avail. This vessel is engaged in the coasting trade
and other ships belonging to the Robert Dollar Co. are
not affected. The S.S. "Esther Dollar", an ocean going
ship, sailed from Shanghai for Pukow on August 10.
page_data.zh: “Agnes Dollar”号轮船于8月5日抵达上海，现租给符拉迪沃斯托克（Vladivostock）的Kunst & Albers公司（音译），该船在江南船坞修理期间，船员于8月8日罢工。公司试图招募新船员的所有尝试均未成功。该船从事沿海贸易，Robert Dollar公司（音译）旗下的其他船只未受影响。“Esther Dollar”号远洋轮船于8月10日从上海驶往浦口。

CENTRAL
August 9 2

Daily Report

D. I. Sullivan

Sir,

No progress towards a settlement of the
dispute between the China Merchants S. N. Co. and the crews
of their ships has yet been made. There are now twelve ships
of the company's ships tied up. The How Chang( ) S. N.
Co. whose offices are at 303 Henan Road, arrived at an
agreement with the Chinese Seamen's Union on August 8. This
company has two ships. Altogether seven companies have
now come to an agreement with the Seamen's Union, and nego-
tiations are in progress between the Union and the San Peh
S. N. Co. The question which is causing the delay with this
company is that the Seamen's Union insist on the company
being signatories of the Hongkong agreement of March 4
last, making the increase of wages retrospective from
January 1 as per the terms of that agreement. There is
still some doubt as to whether the crews of the Dollar Line
ships will strike. The Union claims that they are leaving
it entirely to the men concerned.

招商局轮船公司与其船只船员之间的纠纷尚未取得任何解决进展。目前该公司有十二艘船只停泊。和昌轮船公司（How Chang S. N. Co.，原文括号内缺失，地址河南路303号）于8月8日与中国海员工会达成协议。该公司有两艘船只。截至目前，共有七家公司已与海员工会达成协议，工会与三北轮埠公司（San Peh S. N. Co.）的谈判正在进行中。导致与该公司谈判延误的问题是，海员工会坚持要求该公司签署去年3月4日的香港协议，根据该协议条款，加薪追溯至1月1日生效。Dollar Line（音译）轮船公司的船员是否会罢工仍存疑。工会声称这完全由相关人员自行决定。

REPORT ON Seamen's Strike

Made by D. I. Kay Forwarded by [Signature] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

When at the Seamen's Union headquarters, 163
Broadway, this afternoon I was shown by Tsong Siau Beng
(鐘筱朋), secretary of the Union, three letters which had
been received by the Union from the Robert Dollar Co.,
Standard Oil Co., and the Glen Line Eastern Agencies Ltd.
The letter from the first named company was dated August 5,
whilst the other two are dated August 7. They are all
identical and read as follows :-

"With reference to your several letters to us
"requesting increases of pay for ships crews, we have to
"inform you that this matter is receiving our attention.
"We thank you for your offer of assistance,
"the spirit of which we appreciate. As however, our
"crews will continue to be signed on at the Shipping
"Office of our Consulate, we see no necessity to avail
"ourselves of your kind offices".

Mr. Tsong informed me that this forenoon several
sailors from one of the Dollar boats came to the Union's
offices and asked for instructions as to what action they
should take as they had not received any increase of pay.
He, Mr. Tsong, stated that he informed them that this was a
matter for themselves to decide. When asked by me if he
considered there was any likelihood of this Company's seamen
coming out on strike, he stated it all depended on what
the crews themselves did. The only Dollar Coy steamer in
port at present is the S.S. "Agnes Dollar" which is at present

XXXXXXXXXX Daily Report

D. I. Sullivan

Sir,

A meeting of the board of directors of the China
Merchants Steam Navigation Co. was held on the afternoon of
August 5 when the strike of seamen who demand an increase of
pay of approximately 20% was discussed. The board decided that
in view of the prevailing slump in business they will tie
up all ships the crews of which refuse to go to sea unless
their wages are increased. Business is so bad at present
that the company have been losing money for some months and it
will pay them better to have their ships tied up than working
and carrying cargo at the present freight rates. The board
of directors is meeting continually but nothing further has
been decided upon.

The demands of the Seamen's Union are as follows :-
(1) -a- Crews of Chinese River Boats - 30%
-b- Other Chinese ships below 1,000 tons - 30%
-c- Coasting Vessels - 20%.
(2) All increases of pay shall be retrospective from January 1,
1922.
(3) All seamen shall be paid full wages during the time they
are on strike and no deductions from their wages shall be
made.
(4) After work is resumed the steamship companies shall not
dismiss any member of their crews, and any complaint
should be made to the Seamen's Union. No action to be
taken unless both the Company and the Union agree.
(5) The signing of this agreement by the seamen shall be

8月7日 2时

侦探督察沙利文

先生：

招商局轮船公司董事会于8月5日下午召开会议，讨论了海员要求加薪约20%的罢工事宜。董事会决定，鉴于目前商业萧条，凡拒绝加薪即不肯出海的船员所属船只，一律停航。目前生意极差，公司已连续数月亏损，与其按当前运费率营运载货，不如将船只停泊更为划算。董事会持续开会，但尚未作出进一步决定。

海员工会的要求如下：
(1) -a- 中国内河轮船船员 - 30%
-b- 其他吨位低于1,000吨的中国船只 - 30%
-c- 沿海船只 - 20%。
(2) 所有加薪均自1922年1月1日起追溯生效。
(3) 罢工期间，所有海员应领取全额工资，不得扣除任何工资。
(4) 复工后，轮船公司不得解雇任何船员，如有投诉应向海员工会提出。除非公司与工会双方同意，否则不得采取任何行动。
(5) 海员签署本协议时，须有

page_data.en:
witnessed by an authorized representative of the Seamen's
Union, in the absence of whom the agreement shall not be
effective.

On August 6 the crews of vessels of the following lines
were on strike :-

| Name of Company | No. of Ships |
| :--- | :--- |
| China Merchants Steam Navigation Co. | 11 |
| Ningpo and Shaoshing S. N. Co. | 1 |
| San Poh S. N. Co. | 3 |
| Yu Foong S. N. Co. | 1 |
| Jen Sien S. N. Co. | 1 |

On the night of August 6 the Jen Sien S. N. Co.,
and the Ningpo Shaoshing Steam Navigation Co. sent
representatives to the Seamen's Union offices and an agreement
between the two companies signed and the strike was called off.
The companies admitted to all the Union's demands except
that the increase of pay is only retrospective from July 1.
The captains claimed that they have no agencies in Hongkong
and were not aware of the terms of the Hongkong Agreement.
It is expected that the other smaller Chinese companies will
capitulate soon.

There does not at present appear to be much fear
of any foreign companies becoming involved in the dispute
except perhaps the Glen Line about which the Union officials
are very reticent. There is, however, a danger that if the
China Merchants S. N. Co. remain obdurate the Union may call
page_data.zh:
海员工会授权代表见证，若无代表在场，协议无效。

8月6日，下列公司的船只船员处于罢工状态：

| 公司名称 | 船只数量 |
| :--- | :--- |
| 招商局轮船公司 | 11 |
| 宁波及绍兴轮船公司 | 1 |
| 三北轮船公司 | 3 |
| 裕丰轮船公司 | 1 |
| Jen Sien（音译）轮船公司 | 1 |

8月6日晚，Jen Sien（音译）轮船公司及宁波绍兴轮船公司派代表前往海员工会办事处，两家公司签署了协议，罢工宣告结束。公司接受了工会的所有要求，唯加薪仅自7月1日起追溯生效。船长们声称他们在香港没有代理机构，因此不知晓香港协议的具体条款。预计其他较小的中国公司将很快屈服。

目前看来，外国公司卷入此次纠纷的可能性不大，或许格兰轮船公司除外，工会官员对此事讳莫如深。然而，如果招商局轮船公司继续固执己见，工会可能会号召

page_data.en:
out the employees of all other shipping companies in sympathy.
This will only occur after all other efforts at a settlement
have proved futile.
The Chinese Seamen's Union have opened a branch
office at the Chun Lim Lou( ) teashop, Nanteo Bund,
where a flag bearing an anchor and the characters
( ) meaning Chinese Seamen's Union,
Shanghai Branch, is displayed.
page_data.zh:
其他所有轮船公司的员工举行同情罢工。这种情况只有在所有其他和解努力均告失败后才会发生。
中华海员工会在南市外滩的春霖楼（Chun Lim Lou）茶馆开设了分部办事处，那里悬挂着一面绘有锚图案及意为“中华海员工会上海分会”汉字的旗帜。

Date 7/8/22

Circular issued by the Seamen now on strike-

We hope that all our colleagues will stand firm to the last.

We hope our colleagues will warmly support us.
At this time when people are fully imbued with new
ideas, the labourers are making up and will never bow their
ears or willingly submit to the oppression by capitalists.
Just think; we labourers begin work when the sun rises
and stop when the sun sets and even then our pay is not
sufficient to meet our daily needs.
The brethren engaged in our profession often encounter
high waves and stormy weather and endure hardships far more
severe than any other profession.
This is why the Chinese Seamen's Association presented
the demand for an increase in pay and despite many
difficulties and obstacles our colleagues remained firm and
eventually succeeded in attaining our demands. But in
Shanghai a minority of Shipping hongs would not increase
the pay of their employees. Are the latter not Seamen?
Therefore we demanded that the Coy who has not granted the
increase in accordance with the decision reached at
Hongkong do so accordingly.
The companies however remained unsympathetic in our
suffering and despised our colleagues. Ten days have elapsed
since our letters were sent to them and no reply has been
received. This would indicate that there is no basis for
consultation. Thus we have no alternative but temporarily
to stop work in order to secure a solution by public
opinion.
Colleagues: Be unwaveringly firm:
Be of one mind; Do not give up whilst the strike is on;
Listen to the local branch of the Seamen's Association
which we trust.
Those who disregard the rules of the strike this time
are truly our enemies.
From all the Seamen in Shanghai.

现正罢工的海员发布的通告——

我们希望所有同仁坚持到底。

我们希望同仁们热烈支持我们。
在这个人们充分接受新思想的时代，劳动者正在觉醒，绝不会俯首帖耳或自愿服从资本家的压迫。
试想；我们劳动者日出而作，日落而息，即便如此，我们的薪水仍不足以维持日常所需。
从事我们这一行的弟兄们经常遭遇惊涛骇浪和恶劣天气，承受的艰辛远比其他行业严重。
这就是中华海员协会提出加薪要求的原因，尽管困难重重，障碍多多，我们的同仁依然坚定，最终成功实现了我们的要求。但在上海，少数轮船商号不愿增加员工薪水。难道后者不是海员吗？
因此，我们要求那些未按照香港达成的决定给予加薪的公司照办。
然而，这些公司对我们的苦难无动于衷，蔑视我们的同仁。信件发出至今已十天，未收到任何回复。这表明没有协商的基础。因此，我们别无选择，只能暂时停工，以求通过舆论获得解决。
同仁们：坚定不移：
同心同德；罢工期间不要放弃；
听从我们信任的海员协会本地分会的安排。
此次无视罢工规则的人，确是我们的敌人。
来自上海全体海员。

REPORT ON Seamen's Union (Shanghai Branch) and Seamen's wages.

Made by D. I. Kay Forwarded by [Signature] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

With reference to D. I. Sullivan's report,
attached, I have to state that when visiting the offices of
the Seamen's Union this afternoon I was informed by
Tsong Siau Beng (鐘筱朋), secretary of the Union, that
the communication known as the "third letter" was drafted
by Mr. P. W. Goldring, the Union's legal adviser. It will
be seen that this statement does not agree with that made
to D. I. Sullivan earlier in the day. This letter was sent
to five foreign and 10 Chinese shipping coys by chit book.

Whilst at the Union's Office a boatswain from the
China Merchants S. N. Co. who stated he had been sent by
Mr. Fu Siau En, arrived and discussed the matter of an
increase of wages. He suggested that the best method as
far as his employers were concerned would be for the Union
to send representatives to the Company's offices on Monday
August 7, when the whole matter could be gone into. This
suggestion was agreed to by the Union officials.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Wm. Kay

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by [Signature] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

A visit was paid to the offices of the Chinese
Seamen's Union, Shanghai Branch, this forenoon. There were
about fifteen Chinese present in the office and there appeared
to be more activity there than is usual. In conversation with
Tsoong Siau Bang (鐘筱朋), secretary of the Union, Tsoong
stated that the letter which was sent to the China Merchants
Steam Navigation Co. on August 3, and which was the third letter
sent to that Company by the Union on the question of seamen's
wages, was composed by five representatives of various
seafaring men's Guilds and translated into English by the
secretary of the Guild. I am inclined to doubt this statement
as my impression of Tsoong is that his knowledge of English
is not sufficient to enable him to write these letters, and
I am of opinion that the letter have been written by a
foreigner. However the point is not of any great importance.
The third letter was sent to the China Merchants Steam
Navigation Company by messenger and not by post as stated in
my daily report of to-days date. When asked by me what would
happen if the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company still
ignored the Union's communications, Tsoong stated that it
was in the hands of the Company's employees. Pressed as to
whether the Union would call a strike or what procedure they
would follow, Tsoong was non-committal but stated that the
crews on the China Merchants Steam Navigation Company's ships
might walk out at any moment. When asked how the negotiations
with foreign firms were proceeding Tsoong answered that the

阁下：

今天上午访问了中国海员工会上海分会办事处。办事处内约有十五名华人在场，那里的活动似乎比平时更为活跃。在与该会秘书钟筱邦 (Tsoong Siau Bang) 交谈时，钟称，8月3日发送给招商轮船公司的那封信，即工会就该问题发给该公司的第三封信，是由各航海行会的五名代表起草，并由该行会秘书翻译成英文的。我倾向于怀疑这一说法，因为我对钟的印象是他的英语知识不足以让他写出这些信件，我认为这些信是由外国人撰写的。然而，这一点并不十分重要。第三封信是由信差发送给招商轮船公司的，而非如我今日日报中所述通过邮局发送。当我问及如果招商轮船公司继续无视工会的来函会发生什么情况时，钟表示这取决于该公司的雇员。在被追问工会是否会号召罢工或采取何种程序时，钟未作明确表态，但表示招商轮船公司船只上的船员可能随时离船罢工。当问及与外商的谈判进展如何时，钟回答说

REPORT ON The demand for an increase of Seamen's wages

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by Williams A.J.

Sir,

A second letter, a copy of which is attached, has been sent to local shipping companies by the Shanghai Branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union. Tsoong Siau Bang ( 鍾筱朋 ), Secretary of the Union, states that he himself worded the letter.

Tsoong also states that a reply to their first letter sent on July 25 has been received from the Yu Fong Steamship Co., 12 Peking Road. The reply say that the men employed by the Yu Fong Co. received an increase of pay at the beginning of this year.

When asked what steps the Union proposed to take concerning the reply from the Yu Fong Co., the Secretary of the Union stated that the second letter had not been sent to the Yu Fong Co., but that the men in the Company's employ would be consulted and if they are satisfied no further steps would be taken.

Everything connected with the agitation lends colour to the suspicion that the main object of the Union's present activities is recognition by the shipping firms.

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
J. Sullivan.
D. I.

REPORT ON The demand for increased pay for seamen

Made by D. I. Sullivan Forwarded by [Signature]

Sir,

A reply has been received by the Chinese Seamen's Union, Shanghai Branch, from Messrs Mackenzie & Co. in answer to the former's request for the wages of seamen engaged locally to be raised to a level with the rates ruling in Hongkong. The reply states in effect that Messrs Mackenzie & Co. not being signatories to the Hongkong agreement are not aware of its contents. They, however, believe that their men are paid above the regular rates of pay but that there may be instances which require looking into and these the firm are prepared to consider.

The Glen Line Agencies Ltd. state that they always have two spare crews on hand. They state that during the Hongkong strike their ships ran regularly through Hongkong and none of their crews went on strike and one ship unloaded 800 tons of refrigerator cargo. The company intend to ignore the letter from the Seamen's Union.

After the Hongkong strike the China Merchants Steam Navigation Co. raised the pay of the crews of four of their ships which were running to Hongkong. The pay of the crews of other ships were not increased.

The other foreign shipping lines concerned are considering the matter.

In considering the present demand for increased wages there are many things to be taken into consideration. For instance ships plying on the Upper Yangtze River can obtain all the sailors they require, and very good sailors at that, at $8.00 per month. The Standard Oil Co. send steam

先生：

中国海员工会上海分会已收到麦肯齐公司 (Messrs Mackenzie & Co.) 的复信，答复该会此前关于将在本地雇佣的海员工资提高至与香港现行费率持平的要求。复信大意称，麦肯齐公司并非香港协议的签署方，故不知晓其内容。然而，该公司相信其支付给员工的薪金高于常规费率，但可能存在需要调查的情况，公司准备对此予以考虑。

格兰轮船代理有限公司 (The Glen Line Agencies Ltd.) 表示，他们常备有两支后备船员队伍。该公司称，在香港罢工期间，其船只照常经由香港航行，其船员无人参与罢工，且有一艘船卸载了800吨冷藏货物。该公司打算不予理会海员工会的来信。

香港罢工结束后，招商局轮船公司 (China Merchants Steam Navigation Co.) 提高了其四艘驶往香港的船只船员的薪金。其他船只船员的薪金未予提高。

其他相关外国航运公司正在考虑此事。

在考虑目前增加工资的要求时，有许多因素需加以考量。例如，行驶于长江上游的船只能够以每月8.00美元的价格雇用到所需的所有水手，且其中不乏优秀水手。美孚石油公司 (Standard Oil Co.) 派遣蒸汽

On the other hand deckhands are not so scarce and the work being

a much more difficult task in bringing about a general shipping
strike in Shanghai than they had in Hongkong.

In conversation with the Secretary of the Shanghai
Branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union on July 26, I was informed
confidentially that the letter sent to the shipowners was
composed by Mr. Goldring. It was pointed out to the Secretary
that the Union did not seem to have made sure that the steamship
lines that had been written to were paying less wages than those
ruling in Hongkong. The Secretary intimated that the chief
object of the Union at present was to establish a body who would
be able to negotiate on these matters between the employers and
employees, in other words, recognition by the employers of the
Seamen's Union, and that the question of an increase of
wages is a secondary matter.

Sir,

The officials of the Chinese Seamen's Union
(Shanghai Branch), 163 Broadway, state that about four days
ago sixty representatives of Shanghai seafaring men met at
the above address and after a consultation decided to send a
request to ship owners asking that the pay of Shanghai seamen

The officials of the Union state that there are
about 3,000 members enrolled in the Shanghai branch. This
number includes Shanghai, Tientsin and Ningpo men, Some of them

ascertain from the Union how many of their members are employed
at the various foreign companies to whom letters were sent
but they were unable to supply the information. They did not
appear to have any very definite idea as to how many local
companies had already brought the pay of their employees up
to the Hongkong level. When asked what would happen if the
shipping firms declined to grant the increases of pay, the
officials answered that a vote of seamen would be taken to

Declaration of the Chinese Seamen's Union (Shanghai
Branch) in reference to a demand made by its members for
an increase of wages.

The Chinese Seamen's Union is an organization
composed of all seafaring people in China, all of whom are
entitled to become its members irrespective of the
locality to which they belong. Consequently all members
should enjoy the same benefits and suffer the same
disadvantages. During recent years the cost of living
has increased daily and the wages we previously received
are now insufficient for the support of our parents,
wives and children. At the end of last year, we put
forward a proposal to have our wages increased and
owing to our fellow workers being in a strong position,
we were fortunately successful in attaining our object.
We now understand that some of the steamship companies
in this port have not granted the increase to their
employees, which fact has caused local seamen to protest
against this unfairness, as all Chinese seamen are
supposed to enjoy equal privileges. A few days ago some
of our members (brethren) came to our office and held a
meeting at which they decided to demand an increase of
wages, in accordance with the agreement arrived at in
Hongkong, from those steamship companies which have
so far failed to grant same. Accordingly letters were
on July 25 sent out to the steamship companies concerned.
All our fellow workmen are requested to be patient
until a reply is received. The proverb which says "success
can only be achieved by uniting" is true. Until our
object is attained, we shall not receive equal treatment.
When we are successful, we will be able to receive an
equal amount of pay. Would this not be much better?

中国海员工会（上海分会）关于其会员要求增加工资的声明。

中国海员工会是由中国所有航海人员组成的组织，无论其所属地域如何，均有权成为其会员。因此，所有会员应享受同等利益并承担同等不利条件。近年来，生活成本日益增加，我们此前获得的工资已不足以赡养父母、妻子和儿女。去年年底，我们提出了增加工资的建议，由于工友们处境有利，我们幸而成功达到了目的。现在我们获悉，本港部分轮船公司并未向其员工发放加薪，这一事实引起了本地海员的抗议，认为此举不公，因为所有中国海员理应享有平等特权。几天前，部分会员（兄弟）来到我会办公室并召开会议，决定依据在香港达成的协议，向迄今未能发放加薪的那些轮船公司要求增加工资。据此，有关信件已于7月25日发送给相关轮船公司。恳请全体工友在收到回复之前保持耐心。俗话说“团结才能成功”，此言不虚。在我们达到目的之前，我们将无法受到平等待遇。一旦成功，我们将能够获得同等数额的工资。这岂不是更好吗？

Dear Sirs,

We wish to call your attention to the following facts :—

1.—The above Union has been formed by, and consists of the Chinese members of crews serving on mercantile vessels engaged in the River, Coast and Ocean Trade : and is a Branch of the Chinese Seamen's Union which has been registered in Hongkong.

2.—As is probably well known to you an arrangement was arrived at on March 8th last in Hongkong whereby certain increases in wages or salary were granted to Chinese Seamen. A copy of this agreement in English and Chinese is sent forthwith.

3.—This increase in wages has been adopted by the majority of firms operating from Shanghai with the exception of yours and some others.

4—We therefore feel that we are justified in asking you to come into line with the other companies and that you will, where necessary, communicate with the owners, or agents concerned in order that the men employed in your service may enjoy the same increased rate of pay as those in other employment.

5.—We further ask that such increase may take effect from Jan. 1st 1922 as in the case of other shipping firms and companies.

Yours faithfully,

Chairman
For the Chinese Seamen's Union
SHANGHAI

1. 以1922年1月12日生效的香港工资标准为基础，按下列幅度增加；并自1922年1月1日起适用。
增幅。

4. 其他以港澳轮渡有限公司标准为基准的英国公司内河轮船............................20%

第2条：—将确定一个全面复工的日期。—从离船之时起至该日期止，船员将按照新工资标准领取半薪。船员可复职于其所属公司的任何船只，或经双方同意的其他船只。若上述准备复工的船员无职位空缺，则 agreed 同意在其未受雇期间继续发放半薪，但自全面复工之日起不超过五又二分之一（5½）个月。此半薪将由一名正式任命的管理员所管理的基金进行发放：—

3. 船东同意协助建立一套船员雇佣制度，以尽可能减少与海员工资有关的任何不规范现象：—

I. D.
F. O. 939
4652
28/7/22
Declaration for requesting an increase of wages by members
of the Chinese Seamen Union Association.

The Headquarters of our Chinese Seamen Union Association are established
by all the Chinese seamen in the whole country, with practically no
boundary existed. As all seamen are members, we therefore should all
share either the happiness or hardship. In recent years, our cost of
living becomes much harder, and the wages earned by us are not enough to
support our parents, wife, and children. In order to meet the necessary
demand, we have requested at the end of last year to have our wages
increased. Fortunately, on account of our strong effort, we were
successful in obtaining our good results. As some of the Shipping
Companies, which are smaller than others, have not yet granted any
increase, and in consideration of the fact that our members, the Chinese
seamen, have not enjoyed the similar privilege, we therefore think it
quite unreasonable. Several days ago, our members came to hold a meet-
ing and decided to request those Shipping Companies, which have not yet
granted any increase, to increase our wages in accordance with the
agreement we had formerly made in Hongkong. Our circular letters have
been distributed on the 23rd. inst. notifying all companies. We should
patiently wait for a reply from them, and must use our every effort to
obtain our object, so that we can have the same enjoyment, and it can
also avoid the fact that our members will not earn any insufficient wages.
Is it not good?

中国海员工会会员要求增加工资的宣言。

吾中国海员工会总部由全国所有中国海员共同建立，实际上并无界限之分。鉴于所有海员均为会员，我们理应同甘共苦。近年来，我们的生活成本大幅上升，而我们所赚取的工资不足以赡养父母、妻子和子女。为满足必要之需求，我们已于去年年底提出增加工资的要求。幸赖我们的大力努力，成功取得了良好的结果。由于一些规模较小的航运公司尚未给予任何加薪，且考虑到我们的会员（中国海员）未能享受同等权利，我们认为这极不合理。数日前，我们的会员召开会议，决定要求那些尚未加薪的航运公司，按照我们此前在香港达成的协议增加我们的工资。我们的通告信函已于本月23日分发，通知各公司。我们将耐心等待他们的回复，并必须竭尽全力以实现我们的目标，从而使我们可以享有同等待遇，也可避免我们的会员赚取不足维持生计的工资。这难道不好吗？
